question: Two trains start at the same time from stations P and Q and travel towards each other at the speeds of 75 km/h and 100 km/h, respectively. When they meet, it is found that one train has travelled 50 km more than the other. The distance (in km) between two stations is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of speeds of two trains = 75 : 100 = 3 : 4.

Since time is constant until they meet, Distance ratio = Speed ratio = 3 : 4.

Difference between distances = 4 − 3 = 1 unit.

Given, 1 unit = 50 km.

Total distance (between P and Q) = 3 + 4 = 7 units.

Total distance = 7 × 50 = 350 km.

**∴ The correct answer is 350 km.**
